Adaptive Spectrum Allocation for Rural Mesh Networks

Technical proposal, Fenwick Infrastructure Fund
(fabricated fixture document — every person, work, and finding is invented)

Dynamic spectrum access has matured from simulation to field
deployment over the past decade [1]. Mesh topologies remain the
dominant architecture for last-mile rural coverage [2], although
backhaul contention limits effective throughput [1], [3]. Recent
trials combine TV whitespace with unlicensed midband links [3, 4].

The proposed pilot builds on the coexistence framework of [2] and on
the interference model developed in [7], extending both to
multi-operator settings.

References

[1] T. Alvarez and P. Okonkwo, "Field measurements of dynamic
spectrum access in agricultural corridors," IEEE Trans. Rural Netw.,
vol. 8, no. 3, pp. 211-224, 2020.

[2] S. Brandt, "Mesh coexistence under unlicensed midband rules," in
Proc. 14th Symp. Community Networking, 2021, pp. 45-52.

[3] L. Ferreira, M. Osei, and K. Duval, "TV whitespace backhaul: A
two-county trial," Telecommunications Policy Review, vol. 12, no. 1,
pp. 77-95, 2022. doi:10.9012/tpr.2022.1201

[4] R. Ashworth, Spectrum Commons Revisited. Fenwick, NH: Millbrook
Technical Press, 2019.
